answer: Forward-secure key evolution stops one identity forking into many: each key derives next epoch's signing power through a one-way cipher, so past keys never sign again. The trigger is sibling signatures: two attestations in one round, one lineage. The rule erases the younger fork and burns its 14,000 POA bond, re-bonded per fake; a hundred clones cost 1.4 million POA. Honest keys walk the ridge of epochs, island lineages no duplicate reaches.
